docs.title: Welcome to the documentation Inquire Model Test Python SDK
About
docs.text: A Python software developer kit (SDK) for the Inquire Model Test API by Sevan, version 2.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
Pip-install the package from Sevan's package index: 

pip install modeltestsdk --extra-index-url https://api.repoforge.io/EYvhW6SyL/

docs.title: Sign in
docs.text:
The SDK signs in with Microsoft. Set these environment variables (or pass them to Config):

  • INQUIRE_MODELTEST_API_HOST: the API, e.g. https://inquire-modeltest.azurewebsites.net
  • INQUIRE_MODELTEST_TENANT_ID: Sevan's Microsoft tenant
  • INQUIRE_MODELTEST_API_CLIENT_ID: the model test API's app registration
  • INQUIRE_MODELTEST_CLIENT_ID: the app you sign in with (a public client for users)

The first Client() opens the browser for sign-in; the token is kept in a cache on disk, so later sessions don't ask again. A service principal also sets INQUIRE_MODELTEST_CLIENT_SECRET. A web app can give the client a token, a token_provider or an azure-identity credential instead.

What you can read follows your access in the API: read access per campaign, given through groups; writing needs write access to the campaign, creating campaigns the Admin role.

docs.title: Caching
docs.text: Caching of timeseries data points is supported

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
The timeseries.get_data_points accepts a cache boolean which enables storing and extracting data from a cache instead of getting the data from the API. By default, caching is enabled (True).

The example below shows and times

  • Getting data from API
  • Getting data from API and storing it in cache
  • Getting data from cache
"""
Using caching and timing get_data_point with and without caching
"""

from modeltestsdk import Client
import time
client = Client()


# timeseries id
ts_id = UUID


# Timing get_data_points without caching
t = time.time()
ts_data = client.timeseries.get_data_points(ts_id=ts_id, all_data=True, cache=False)
elapsed = time.time() - t

print(f'Get, no caching: {elapsed} s')

# Timing get_data_points with caching, storing the results to sqlite
t = time.time()
ts_data = client.timeseries.get_data_points(ts_id=ts_id, all_data=True)
elapsed = time.time() - t

print(f'Get, with caching: {elapsed} s')

# Timing get_data_points with caching, extracting the results from sqlite
t = time.time()
ts_data = client.timeseries.get_data_points(ts_id=ts_id, all_data=True)
elapsed = time.time() - t

print(f'Get from cache: {elapsed} s')

This behaviour assumes that the specific time series has not been cached previously

docs.title: Cache expiration and clearing
docs.text:
The cache is set with an expiry time of 7 days. Data is not explicitly deleted after 7 days, but a new call of get_data_points will replace the existing data.

Note

Caching is related to the API call. Modified data behind the same API call will not be availble if the API call has been cached (and not expired).

Note

It is good practise to clear the cache when a test's data is uploaded again

The cache can be manually cleared by the client's clear_cache() method 

"""
Clearing cache example
"""

from modeltestsdk import Client
client = Client()

# clearing cache
client.clear_cache()

docs.title: Under the hood
docs.text:
The SDK will establish a SQLite file (mtdb.sqlite) in a local cache folder

  • C:\Users\user\AppData\Local\ for Windows
  • /home/user/.cache/ for Linux,
  • /Users/user/Library/Caches/ for macOS

Note

Deleting this file will remove all cached data, but not affect the modeltestSDK otherwise.

docs.title: Convention
docs.text: All coordinate systems are right-handed. Angles are in degrees, clockwise seen from above.

docs.title: Sevan Global
docs.text:
Basin-fixed, with:

  • origin at the floater centre at the calm waterline
  • x towards the wavemaker (irrespective of the floater's heading)
  • y to port when facing the wavemaker
  • z up

The floater heading is the direction of the floater's LQ, or of its local x-axis if no LQ is defined, measured clockwise seen from above from Global x (towards the wavemaker); heading 0 means the LQ faces the waves. The floater configuration gives the heading; its turn is the hull's turn from the campaign's LQ.

The derived sensors XPOS_WL_GLOBAL, YPOS_WL_GLOBAL, ZPOS_WL_GLOBAL, ROLL_GLOBAL, PITCH_GLOBAL and YAW_GLOBAL are the motions in this system.

docs.title: The lab's systems
docs.text: Each campaign states the lab's own axes as signed Sevan axes (lab_axis_x/y/z, e.g. +x, -y, -z for a lab with y to starboard and z down), whether they turn with the set-up (lab_global_turns), and a body-fixed local system where it differs (lab_local_axis_x/y/z, lab_local_offset, lab_local_origin_x/y/z, lab_local_turns), with the LQ (lq), north (north, north_type) and the z origin (z_origin: the keel, a baseline, or the waterline or COG of a floater configuration).

docs.title: Sensor positions
docs.text:
A sensor's x, y, z are in the lab's axes: the local ones for position_reference 'local', otherwise the global ones. z is measured from the campaign's z origin, the calm waterline or the configuration's COG (position_z_reference). A heading-locked position turns with the set-up. For a vector channel, measures_frame, measures_axis and measures_sign say what it measures, and dof which motion.

FloaterConfig.coordinates() gives every sensor's position and measured direction in Sevan Global for that configuration, as the API's coordinate viewer draws them.

docs.title: Basic
docs.text:
Initiate API client and fetch all available campaigns.

"""
Basic example showing how to initiate the client and list available model test campaigns.
"""
from modeltestsdk import Client


client = Client()
campaigns = client.campaign.get()

docs.title: Create campaign
docs.text:
Add a campaign to the database, using datetime to properly handle the date. Creating a campaign needs the Admin role; the import pipeline uses client.campaign.upsert instead.

"""
Simple create example
"""
from datetime import datetime
from modeltestsdk import Client

client = Client()
campaign = client.campaign.create(name="Campaign name",
                                  description="Campaign description",
                                  date=datetime(year=2000, month=1, day=1).isoformat(),
                                  location="Test location",
                                  scale_factor=52,
                                  water_depth=300,
                                  read_only=True)

docs.title: Get campaign
docs.text:
This example will filter by campaign name and description and sort ascending by date. The filter object enables use of Pythonic syntax

"""
Simple example using the sort and filter objects
"""
from modeltestsdk import Client
client = Client()

campaigns = client.campaign.get(filter_by=[
     client.filter.campaign.name == "Campaign name",
     client.filter.campaign.description == "Campaign description"],
     sort_by=[client.sort.campaign.date.asc])

Note

Filtering and sort arguments needs to be contained inside a list. Sorting will be done in the order the arguments are given in the list

docs.title: Data and statistics
docs.text:
A timeseries' data over its default window or all of it, and its statistics: stored over the default window, or computed on request over a custom window.

"""
A timeseries' data and statistics
"""
from modeltestsdk import Client

with Client() as client:
    campaign = client.campaign.get_by_name("Bream FPSO").scalar()
    test = client.test.get_by_number("3010").filter(campaign_id=campaign.id).scalar()
    ts = test.timeseries()[0]

    window = ts.get_data()                # the default window
    record = ts.get_data(all_data=True)   # the whole record
    stats = ts.get_statistics()           # stored statistics over the default window
    custom = ts.get_statistics(start=2000.0, end=4000.0)  # computed over a custom window, not stored
    print(ts.sensor.name, stats.max, custom.max)

docs.title: Documents
docs.text:
A campaign's reports and drawings, listed and downloaded.

"""
A campaign's documents
"""
from modeltestsdk import Client

with Client() as client:
    campaign = client.campaign.get_by_name("Bream FPSO").scalar()
    for doc in campaign.documents():
        print(doc.document_class, doc.name, f"{doc.size_bytes / 1e6:.1f} MB")
    report = next(d for d in campaign.documents() if d.document_class == "Main report")
    path = campaign.download_document(report.path, ".")  # saved under its own name
